Also because QR ≅ RS, triangle RQS is an isosceles triangle, with the vertex angle at R being 72°, therefore the base angles ∠RQS and ∠QSR are each (180−72)/2 = 54°. raw_record.question_text: If $\overline{P Q} \cong \overline{Q S}$, $\overline{Q R} \cong \overline{R S}$, and $m\angle PRS = 72$, what is the measure of $\angle QPS$?

method.method_draft: Use a direct angle chase. From the image, note that R, Q, and P are collinear in the order R-Q-P, and S is connected to R, Q, and P. Therefore ray RQ lies on ray RP, so ∠QRS is the same angle as ∠PRS. From the text, m∠PRS = 72 and QR ≅ RS, so triangle RQS is isosceles with vertex angle 72 at R. Its base angles at Q and S are each (180−72)/2 = 54. Since QR and QP are opposite rays on the straight base line, ∠RQS and ∠SQP form a linear pair, so ∠SQP = 180−54 = 126. From the text, PQ ≅ QS, so triangle PQS is isosceles with vertex angle 126 at Q, making the base angles at P and S equal. Thus ∠QPS = (180−126)/2 = 27.

method.method_draft: Use an algebraic variable angle chase starting from the target. From the image, R, Q, and P lie on one straight line with Q between R and P, and S is joined to all three points. Let x = m∠QPS. From the text, PQ ≅ QS, so in triangle PQS the base angles at P and S are equal: ∠QPS = ∠QSP = x. Hence ∠PQS = 180−2x. Because QP and QR are opposite rays in the image, ∠RQS = 180−∠PQS = 2x. From the text, QR ≅ RS, so triangle RQS is isosceles and ∠RQS = ∠QSR = 2x. Therefore ∠QRS = 180−4x. The image shows RQ lies along RP, so ∠QRS = ∠PRS, and the text gives ∠PRS = 72. Solve 180−4x = 72 to get x = 27, so ∠QPS = 27.
